tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Free. Before an agent spends money or time on a URL: is it allowed (robots.txt for this service and, if you pass user_agent, for your own bot; Content Signals such as ai-input and ai-train; meta robots), does a bot check or sign-in stand in the way, and which engine each task needs — plain fetch, Ki

tools.name: read
tools.description: Returns the main content of a web page as clean Markdown with absolute links. Tries the cheapest way that works: plain fetch, then Kitesurf, then Chromium, and reports which one worked. Refuses (and charges nothing) when the site's robots.txt or Content Signals say no, or when a bot check answers in

tools.name: actions
tools.description: Returns the forms (with every field, its label and whether it is required), buttons and links on a page, each with a CSS selector an automation tool can use. Uses the rendered page when the HTML alone has none. Charged only on success. Price: US$0.004 per successful call (API key credits or x402).

tools.name: extract
tools.description: No AI model involved: returns the structured data the page already publishes — JSON-LD / schema.org objects (products, articles, events, organisations, breadcrumbs), prices and offers, meta and Open Graph tags, canonical URL, language versions, licence, RSS/Atom/JSON feeds, and HTML data tables as c

tools.name: delta
tools.description: For pages an agent checks again and again. The first call returns the page as sections plus a fingerprint; send that fingerprint back as "previous" next time and get only the sections that changed (and the headings of removed ones), or changed:false. tools.name: site
tools.description: Free. Everything an agent should know about a website before using it: its llms.txt (and llms-full.txt), sitemap (page count and first URLs), feeds, language versions, Content Signals, and which known AI crawlers and agents its robots.txt allows. Rate-limited per IP.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: PNG screenshot of a page at 1280×800 (or the full page). engine "auto" uses Kitesurf unless the page needs video or WebGL, then Chromium. Charged only on success. Price: US$0.008 per successful call (API key credits or x402).

tools.name: credits
tools.description: Free. Credits remaining on the API key sent in the Authorization header (1 credit = US$0.001).

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "site" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Free. Everything an agent should know about a website before using it: its llms.txt (and llms-full.txt), sitemap (page count and first URLs), feeds, language ve…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "credits" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Free. Credits remaining on the API key sent in the Authorization header (1 credit = US$0.001).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: preflight, read, extract · Private data: read, actions, extract, delta, screenshot, credits · Public sink: delta.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: preflight, read, extract · Private data: read, actions, extract, delta, screenshot, credits · Public sink: delta

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
